description: Utah-only rules checked against the Utah Code and the Driver License Division. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines. The adult per se concentration in section 41-6a-502 is .05 grams, not .08.

questions.q: The lawful speed Utah Code states for a reduced speed school zone is
questions.explanation: Section 41-6a-601(2)(a) says 20 miles per hour is lawful in a reduced speed school zone as defined in section 41-6a-303. Section 41-6a-604(1) separately says an individual may not operate a vehicle at a speed greater than 20 miles per hour in that zone.

questions.q: Subject to the basic speed rule and the posted-limit sections, the lawful speed Utah states for an urban district is
questions.explanation: Section 41-6a-601(2)(b) says 25 miles per hour is lawful in any urban district. Subsection (2)(c) says 55 miles per hour is lawful in other locations. A speed over those limits, or over a limit set under sections 41-6a-602 and 41-6a-603, is prima facie evidence that the speed is not reasonable or prudent, except as provided in section 41-6a-604.

questions.q: Where section 41-6a-601 does not set a lower urban or school speed, the lawful speed in other Utah locations is
questions.explanation: Section 41-6a-601(2)(c) says 55 miles per hour is lawful in other locations, subject to the basic speed rule and to limits established under sections 41-6a-602 and 41-6a-603.

questions.q: A posted speed limit that the Utah Department of Transportation sets on a freeway or other limited-access highway
options: May not exceed 75 mph without a study
Is 80 mph on every freeway with no study
Is unlawful unless it is exactly 65 mph
questions.explanation: Section 41-6a-602(3) says that except as provided for freeways, a posted speed limit may not exceed 65 mph. On a freeway or other limited-access highway, a posted limit may not exceed 75 mph, except that the Department of Transportation may establish a posted limit above that 75 mph ceiling if it is based on a highway traffic engineering and safety study.

questions.q: Utah's driving-under-the-influence statute uses a blood or breath alcohol concentration of
options: .02 grams or greater for every driver
questions.explanation: Section 41-6a-502(1) says a person commits driving under the influence by operating or being in actual physical control of a vehicle with a blood or breath alcohol concentration of .05 grams or greater at the time of the test, or .05 grams or greater at the time of operation or actual physical control, or while under the influence to a degree that makes the person incapable of safely operating a vehicle. Concentration is grams per 100 milliliters of blood or grams per 210 liters of breath.

questions.q: An individual younger than 21 may not operate or be in actual physical control of a vehicle in Utah with
options: A blood or breath concentration of .08 or greater only
Any measurable alcohol shown by a chemical test
A concentration of .05 or greater only
A concentration of .02 or greater only
questions.explanation: Section 53-3-231(2)(a), effective July 1, 2026, says an individual younger than 21 may not operate or be in actual physical control of a vehicle or motorboat with any measurable blood, breath, or urine alcohol concentration in the individual's body as shown by a chemical test.

questions.q: An alcohol-restricted driver who operates or is in actual physical control of a vehicle in Utah violates section 41-6a-530 by having
options: .05 or more only if the driver is under 18
questions.explanation: Section 41-6a-530(1) says an alcohol-restricted driver who operates or is in actual physical control of a vehicle with any measurable or detectable amount of alcohol in the body is guilty of a class B misdemeanor. A separate rule, section 53-3-231, prohibits a driver younger than 21 from operating a vehicle with any measurable alcohol concentration shown by a chemical test.

questions.q: The Utah Driver License Division says a driver age 20 or under may be suspended or denied for 30 days to a year after accumulating
options: 70 or more points in three years
questions.explanation: The Driver License Division points page says that if a driver 20 or under accumulates 70 or more points in three years, the driver may be suspended or denied for 30 days to a year. It says an adult who accumulates 200 or more points in three years may be suspended for three months to a year.

questions.q: On the Utah Driver License Division chart, speeding 1 to 10 mph over the limit is assessed
questions.explanation: The division's chart lists 35 points for speeding 1 to 10 mph over, 55 points for 11 to 20 mph over, and 75 points for 21 mph over. Reckless driving is 80 points and careless driving is 50 points.

questions.q: If a Utah driver goes one full year without a moving-violation conviction, the division
options: Leaves the point total unchanged until three convictions
questions.explanation: The Driver License Division says that when a driver goes one full year without a moving-traffic-violation conviction, half the points are removed. Two successive years without a conviction remove all points. Points for a conviction are also removed three years after the violation date. An approved defensive-driving course may be used once every three years and reduces the total by a maximum of 50 points.

questions.q: A Utah learner permit may be issued to an applicant who is at least
questions.explanation: Section 53-3-210.5 says the division may issue a learner permit effective for 18 months to an applicant who is at least 15, and the Driver License Division states the same minimum age. For ages 15 to 17, the division says the permit must be held six months and until age 16.

questions.q: The person who signs a Utah minor's application for a provisional license must certify practice driving of
options: At least 40 hours, of which at least 10 hours were after sunset
50 hours, including 10 hours in inclement weather
180 days of driving with no hour count
questions.explanation: Section 53-3-211 requires the person who signs a minor's provisional-license application to certify that, under a permit, the minor completed at least 40 hours of driving, of which at least 10 hours were during night hours after sunset. The Driver License Division lists the same 40 hours, with 10 after sunset.

questions.q: A Utah learner-permit holder younger than 18 may drive a class D vehicle only if the person beside the driver is
options: Any licensed driver who is at least 18
An instructor, licensed parent, or authorized adult 21+
No one; the permit allows driving alone in daylight
questions.explanation: Section 53-3-210.5 and the Driver License Division limit a learner under 18 to driving with an approved driving instructor, a licensed parent or legal guardian, or the responsible adult who signed for financial responsibility beside the driver. A parent or legal guardian who is not licensed may authorize an individual 21 or older to occupy that seat.

questions.q: Utah's nighttime restriction for licensed drivers ages 16 and 17 prohibits driving
options: Between midnight and 5 a.m., with exceptions
Between 9 p.m. and 6 a.m. with no exceptions
Between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. only on interstates
At no hour; only a passenger limit applies
questions.explanation: The Driver License Division says licensed drivers ages 16 and 17 may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m. unless accompanied by a licensed driver 21 or older, traveling to or from work, in an emergency, in agricultural operations, or for school-sponsored activities.

questions.q: For the first six months, or until age 18, a Utah driver ages 16 or 17 may not drive with non-immediate family members unless
options: The trip is under five miles
questions.explanation: The Driver License Division says that for the first six months or until age 18, the driver cannot drive with non-immediate family members unless a licensed driver at least 21 is sitting in the passenger seat, the driving is for agricultural operations, or the driver is responding to an emergency.

questions.q: In Utah, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Utah requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Utah complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Utah requires 40 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Utah teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Utah requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

questions.q: In Utah, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Utah, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Utah not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Utah restricts provisional drivers from Midnight to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

questions.q: In Utah, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Utah drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

provenance.manual: Teen Driver Restrictions | Utah Driver License Division

questions.q: How many questions are on the Utah car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Utah car knowledge test has 50 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Utah car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Utah car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Utah, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Utah, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.05% or more.

questions.q: In Utah, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Utah sets the under-21 limit at 0.00%.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Utah residential district?
questions.explanation: Utah sets 25 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Utah?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Utah can be posted up to 80 mph for cars.

questions.q: How is Utah's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
No seat belt law for adults
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: Utah seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Utah?
questions.explanation: Utah requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

questions.q: What is Utah's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Utah requires at least $30,000 / $65,000 / $25,000.

questions.q: Under Utah's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Utah can suspend an adult's license at 200 points in 36 months.

provenance.manual: Utah Points System | Utah Driver License Division
